newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador steps up Venezuelan sugar import fight.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador steps up Venezuelan sugar import fight.

text.p: Government ministers and Salvadoran businessmen will fly to Caracas on Monday to step up their campaign to reverse a Venezuelan decision to ban sugar imports, the Deputy Economy Minister said Thursday.
Heading the delegation will be Agriculture Minister Manuel Gutierrez and Juan Interiano, the director of the National Sugar Association, Rene Leon told reporters.

Venezuela suspended temporarily sugar imports from Central America and Andean nations on September 23 because they claimed they had high inventories in domestic warehouses. Importers say the move was protectionist.
According to government statistics, Salvadoran imports were expected to close 1996 at 26,000 tonnes, down from the 31,952 tonnes imported by Venezuela in 1995.
Leon told reporters that El Salvador hoped to free up some 6,000 tonnes of sugar currently frozen in Venezuelan ports.
The temporary ban not only affects Salvadoran sugar but also imports from Guatemala, Nicaragua, Colombia, Ecuador and Bolivia.
